about: MUTATING — prove ONE node's gate volume is the gate disk and write the marker /gate-runs/.gate-volume that infra/gate-runner/run.sh's gate-disk guard refuses every gate without (infra/forge/prove-gate-volume.sh <node>; backlog ae59464b, door 3 of 3 of the w-1 gate-volume move). Asked for by David on 88b35891 (david_steer_20261106_1559Z: 'our control should be sufficient to manage moving the workloads') and ordered on 2026-11-07 ~02:00Z ('go ahead with the gate volume move'); it is authorised as a door only by the release of its held trust-boundary car after its adversarial review. WHAT IT DOES: through the forge's ops_kubectl door it creates Job boss-dev/gate-volume-proof from THIS checkout's infra/gate-runner/gate-volume-proof.yaml, the node substituted and nothing else; the pod mounts claim gate at /gate-seed and /gate-runs as the gate container does, runs as 65534:1500 with fsGroup 1500 in the gate's own image, and is pinned to the node. Its script reads the devices of /gate-seed, /gate-runs and /etc/hosts (EPHEMERAL) and refuses, writing nothing, when the seed and the runs directory differ or the runs directory is EPHEMERAL's; writes a file and reads its owner back as 65534:1500; cp --reflink=always seed to runs and cmp; prints df; and only then writes the marker by rename — date, node, device, filesystem type and source — and reads it back. The verb waits (the Job's 300 s deadline plus 60 s), prints the pod's WHOLE log, and judges it again rather than trusting it: the effect line PROVEN <node> device <n> marker /gate-runs/.gate-volume is printed only when the Job is Complete, its pod exited 0 on the named node, the log carries one devices line with seed and runs equal and not EPHEMERAL's, one PROOF-OK line, and one marker line naming that node and that device; anything else is FAILED, exit 1, with the log above it. THE BOUND IS THE SCRIPT'S (cluster-node-lib.sh) AND REFUSES, CREATING NOTHING (exit 78): the node must be one DNS label, a talos-worker the estate registry declares once, and the cluster must agree (no control-plane label, the registry's address) — a control plane is refused before any door opens; the node must not be cordoned; claim boss-dev/gate must exist and be Bound, to a PersistentVolume whose node affinity names this node; no gate may be in flight (a pod in boss-dev not Succeeded or Failed that mounts the claim, or an unfinished Job labelled app=gate-runner) — the proof would race a workspace on the volume it judges, so the move holds gate launches first; and no UNFINISHED Job named gate-volume-proof may stand — a running proof may be writing the marker and is never touched. IT REMOVES ONE JOB, AND ONLY A FINISHED PREVIOUS PROOF: the name is fixed, so the API server itself refuses a second proof while one stands, and a finished one would stand for its ttlSecondsAfterFinished, an hour (the floor every_job_bounds_its_finished_history.rs holds every Job to, so a failed Job's log outlives it) — too long for a retry to wait while every gate is stopped. So a previous proof standing Complete or Failed has its WHOLE log printed onto this run first (capture before delete, the log the TTL exists to keep), is deleted with DeleteOptions preconditions.uid set to the uid just read (a name that changed hands is refused by the API server, never deleted), and is read back gone before anything is created; a refused delete, or one not read back gone, is FAILED with nothing created. It is declared in the tree, so delete-orphan-object refuses it by design: this is the one door that removes it early. NO PASSKEY, decided on backlog ae59464b and stated here for its review: (1) it is ONE bounded write — the tree's own Job, whose only caller-supplied word is a node the registry and the cluster bound, and a marker written only after the pod has proven the layout run.sh's guard compares; (2) the marker's absence stops every gate and its presence only lets them run, and run.sh still compares the devices on every gate whatever the marker says, so the worst case is a marker on a volume this proof could not tell from the gate disk — which a passkey would not catch either, since the approver reads the same device numbers the script judges; (3) it adds no capability: `boss gate` creates Jobs in boss-dev mounting the same claim, as the same uid, gid and fsGroup, in the same image, many times a day unattended, and this pod does a strict subset of what any gate's code can do through /gate-runs; (4) a plan would render nothing an approver could judge beyond the node and the tree's file, both bound here (CLAUDE.md Diagnosis: reads and bounded reclaims are mechanical, destructive-by-policy actions are not; trim-build-node is the precedent). The destructive steps of the move — retiring the user volume, wiping the partition, converging the node — are the ones that carry passkeys; this is the step after them. A precedent for the PROCESS, not a loosened default: a verb that writes anything else onto a volume, or takes more than a node from the packet, earns no passkey-free door from this one. TIMEOUT 900: the Job's deadline (300 s, read by the script from the manifest) and the wait's 60 s margin, the door's first-time image pull (120 s), about a dozen kubectl reads bounded at 20-30 s each, and — when a finished previous proof is removed — its log read, the delete, and up to six read-backs of its name. Pinned by crates/core/boss-testing/tests/prove_gate_volume_sh.rs.
effect: ^prove-gate-volume: PROVEN [a-z0-9-]+ device [0-9]+ marker /gate-runs/[.]gate-volume — Job [a-z0-9-]+ completed on [a-z0-9-]+, and its log reads the marker back: proven .+$
